A docs#FrameHom can only be defined between two CompleteLattices:

/-- The type of frame homomorphisms from `α` to `β`. They preserve finite meets and arbitrary joins.
-/
structure FrameHom (α β : Type*) [CompleteLattice α] [CompleteLattice β] extends
  InfTopHom α β where
  /-- The proposition that frame homomorphisms commute with arbitrary suprema/joins. -/
  map_sSup' (s : Set α) : toFun (sSup s) = sSup (toFun '' s)

Wouldn't [SupSet α] [Min α] [Top α] [SupSet β] [Min β] [Top β] work just as well? Is there a reason other than simplicity to require a CompleteLattice? I am asking because I have a Function (which satisfies the condiitions of FrameHom) between two types which don't have a complete Lattice Structure (no sensible InfSet)
if we generalize this away from complete lattices it shouldn't use sSup because of junk values
(Would a PR which weakens these assumptions (also in other structures and typeclasses) be accepted?)

Aaron Liu said:

if we generalize this away from complete lattices it shouldn't use sSup because of junk values

What do you mean by junk values?
we should use docs#IsLUB instead when generalizing away from complete lattices
Would using docs#CompleteSemilatticeSup together with [Min] and [Top] be an option?

Aaron Liu said:

we should use docs#IsLUB instead when generalizing away from complete lattices

I'm not really generalizing away from CompleteLattices here because every CompleteSemilatticeSup is technically a Complete Lattice but I don't want that instance because the sInf does not make sense.

Aaron Liu said:

going to CompleteSemilatticeSup isn't actually more general

Would it make sense to properly generalize this? How would this work with docs#IsLUB ?
I'm not sure what you mean about sInf not making sense

Christian Krause said:

Aaron Liu said:

going to CompleteSemilatticeSup isn't actually more general

Would it make sense to properly generalize this? How would this work with docs#IsLUB ?

no idea, I don't work with FrameHoms so I don't know what the proper generalization would be

Aaron Liu said:

I'm not sure what you mean about sInf not making sense

I am trying to build API for the Closed Sublocales over a Frame X. Each Closed Sublocale corresponds to one Element of X (like the Open Sublocales) and the Order of the Closeds is defined dually to that of X. (Which lines up with the corresponding Sublocales, i.e. the embedding from Closeds into Sublocales is Monotone). InfSet and Max on the closed are also defined through their corresponding element, which also lines up with the Sublocales (i.e. the embedding from Closeds into Sublocales could be called a CoFrameHom (commutes with sInf and sup)). But this embedding does not commute with sSup, so a sSup operation on Closeds would make no sense, because the infinite intersection of closed sublocales is not always closed.

I don't know what a closed sublocale is but note that in mathlib we usually still define a sSup operation even when it doesn't commute with coercion (for example, docs#Subgroup and docs#TopologicalSpace.Closeds both have a sSup)
Ok, if docs#TopologicalSpace.Closeds have sSup, Closed Sublocales (which are somewhat similar) should probably also have one. Thanks for the hint!
